intent: A cafe owner adding cappuccino to the cash register menu
rationale: Made and served on premises, so the catering code for coffee drinks, not a packaged-coffee goods code such as Torabika or Nescafe cappuccino sachets.

intent: A coffee shop adding latte to its menu
rationale: A coffee-based drink prepared by the barista: catering 'coffee and coffee-containing drinks'.

intent: A coffee shop adding americano to its menu
rationale: Brewed on premises; same catering coffee-drinks code as any espresso drink.

intent: A tea house (choyxona) selling a pot of green tea
rationale: Tea brewed and served in the establishment is the catering 'teas' drink code; the green-tea goods code (00902001001) is for selling packs of tea leaves.

intent: A cafe selling homemade lemonade by the glass or jug
rationale: Catering 'other soft drinks (compotes, kvass, mors, lemonades...)'; the bottled soft-drink goods codes are for resold bottles.

intent: A cafe squeezing fresh orange juice to order
rationale: Freshly squeezed juice made on premises falls under the catering 'other soft drinks' line, not the packaged juice goods code 02009001006.

intent: A cafe blending smoothies to order
rationale: A non-alcoholic drink made on premises that is neither tea nor coffee: catering 'other soft drinks'.

intent: A restaurant or osh markazi selling a portion of plov
rationale: Plov is a main course cooked with meat, so 'main dishes with meat'. 'Main dishes from vegetables, grains and pasta' is defensible because rice is the bulk of the dish (and is right for a meatless plov).

intent: A restaurant grilling shashlik skewers
rationale: Shashlik is a meat main course (lamb or beef by default). Chicken shashlik would take the poultry main-dish code, so both are acceptable for the bare word.

intent: A tea house baking samsa in a tandoor and selling them by the piece
rationale: Samsa is a baked dough item with filling, which fits 'main dishes, flour-based'. 'Fast food' is defensible for samsa sold as street food. Not the bread code: samsa is a filled pastry, not bread.

intent: A cafe adding lagman to its menu
rationale: Most Tashkent menus list plain lagman under first courses (noodles in broth), hence soups. Fried (qovurma) lagman is a main dish with meat or with pasta; the bare word cannot tell which, so all three are defensible.

intent: A restaurant selling steamed manti
rationale: Manti are dough dumplings with a meat filling: 'main dishes, flour-based' fits best; 'main dishes with meat' is also defensible.

intent: A fast-food stall selling shawarma
rationale: Prepared on site and sold as fast food: catering 'fast food'. A supermarket reselling ready shawarma would use 02106999032 instead.

intent: A fast-food kiosk selling hot dogs
rationale: Assembled on site: catering 'fast food'.

intent: A pizzeria selling a pepperoni pizza
rationale: Pizza is usually treated as fast food; 'main dishes, flour-based' is equally defensible for a sit-down pizzeria.

intent: A sushi bar selling a Philadelphia roll set
rationale: Rolls with salmon are a fish dish: 'main dishes with fish and seafood'. 'Snacks with fish and seafood' is defensible when rolls are served as a starter.

intent: A restaurant adding Caesar salad to the menu
rationale: Catering 'salads prepared in the establishment'. Supermarket deli salads use 02106999033 instead.

intent: A canteen selling a bowl of borscht
rationale: Catering 'soups prepared in the establishment'.

intent: A cafe selling cake by the slice
rationale: Catering 'desserts, confectionery, sold (including prepared) in the establishment'. The wording covers cakes bought in from a bakery and sliced in the cafe, so it is still the catering code, not the cake goods code 01905007001.

intent: A cafe serving scoops of ice cream in a bowl
rationale: Served as a dessert in the cafe: catering desserts. Ice cream is not strictly confectionery, so 'desserts, other' is the better fit, but 'desserts, confectionery' is a common and defensible choice. Packaged ice cream resold from a freezer would be 02105001004.

intent: A restaurant selling a fixed-price business lunch set
rationale: A set meal at lunchtime: catering 'complex meal rations, lunches'.

intent: A cafe selling a set breakfast
rationale: A set breakfast: catering 'complex meal rations, breakfasts'. A single egg dish ordered on its own would be 'main dishes from eggs' instead.

intent: A restaurant adding a delivery charge line for its own food to the receipt
rationale: The catering code 'other services, delivery of food prepared in the establishment' is exactly this. The general 'food delivery service' code (10112006004) is defensible, but it is meant for courier and delivery companies.

intent: A lounge cafe charging for a hookah
rationale: Catering 'other services, preparing a ready hookah for smoking in the establishment'. Hookah tobacco sold in packs would be a tobacco goods code.

intent: A burger place selling French fries
rationale: Fries sold on their own in a fast-food place are fast food; as a side dish in a restaurant they are 'garnishes, sauces and toppings'. Both are defensible.

intent: A restaurant selling a cold meat platter as a starter
rationale: Catering 'snacks with meat'.

intent: A bar mixing a Margarita cocktail
rationale: Catering 'alcoholic cocktails of all kinds prepared in the establishment'. Spirits sold by the bottle keep their marked alcohol goods codes.

intent: A restaurant adding a 10% service charge to the bill
rationale: Catering 'other services, service charge in the establishment'.

intent: An Uzbek-speaking owner of an osh centre adding plov to the till
rationale: 'Osh' is plov: meat main dish, with the grains main-dish code defensible as for 'плов'.

intent: A choyxona selling a pot of green tea
rationale: Tea brewed in the establishment: catering 'teas'.

intent: A restaurant selling kazan kabob (fried meat with potatoes)
rationale: A meat main course.

intent: A canteen selling mastava (rice soup)
rationale: Catering 'soups'.

intent: A restaurant selling tandoor bread with meals
rationale: Catering 'bread and bread products sold (including prepared) in the establishment'. A shop reselling non would use the goods code 01905002007 (lepyoshka).

intent: A choyxona selling achichuk (tomato and onion salad)
rationale: Catering 'salads'.

intent: An owner typing in Uzbek Cyrillic adding plov to the menu
rationale: Same dish as 'плов'/'osh': meat main dish, grains main dish defensible.

intent: A restaurant selling shurpa (meat soup)
rationale: Catering 'soups'.

intent: A restaurant selling manti, typed in Uzbek Cyrillic
rationale: Same as 'манты': flour-based main dish, meat main dish defensible.

intent: A tea house selling tea with lemon
rationale: Tea brewed in the establishment: catering 'teas'.

intent: A coffee shop whose POS menu is in English adding cappuccino
rationale: Made on premises: catering coffee drinks, not a packaged cappuccino-sachet goods code.

intent: A burger bar adding a cheeseburger to its menu
rationale: Catering 'fast food'.

intent: A corner shop reselling packs of baby diapers
rationale: Generic query, so the category-level 'Подгузники' code; a known brand (Pampers, Huggies...) would take its branded code under the same sub-position.

intent: A kiosk reselling Winston Blue cigarette packs
rationale: Cigarettes with filter have no unbranded or category-level code, so the branded code is required. Winston Blue is listed twice ('Winston Blue' and 'Blue', different barcodes); either matches the product, the barcode on the pack decides.

intent: A grocery reselling one-litre packs of milk
rationale: No brand given, so the category-level 'Молоко' code; the pack size is not part of the classification.

intent: A corner shop reselling loaves of bread from a local bakery
rationale: 'Хлеб (буханка)' is the plain loaf; 'Прочие виды хлеба' is defensible for other breads. Not the cafe bread code: nothing is served on premises.

intent: A grocery selling sugar
rationale: Packaged sugar is 'Сахар упакованный'; sugar sold loose by weight is 'Сахар весовой'. The query does not say which.

intent: A grocery reselling bottled vegetable oil
rationale: 'Растительное масло' on a label is usually sunflower or cottonseed oil, or a blend; the catalog has no single 'vegetable oil' code, so sunflower, cottonseed and mixed vegetable oils are all acceptable.

intent: A shop reselling bottled mineral water
rationale: The catalog has no 'mineral water' sub-position: mineral waters sit under sparkling or still water depending on carbonation (Chortoq is sparkling, many table waters are still).

intent: A shop reselling 1.5 L bottles of Coca-Cola
rationale: Branded code required for the specific bottle. Coca-Cola 1.5 L PET appears twice ('сладкий, ПЭТ бутылка 1,5 л' and 'газированный сладкий пэт бутылка 1,5 л', different barcodes); both describe the product.

intent: A kiosk reselling energy drinks
rationale: Category-level 'Энергетический напиток'.

intent: A cosmetics shop reselling shampoo
rationale: Category-level 'Шампунь (всех видов)'; children's shampoo (03305005002) and car shampoo are different products.

intent: A pharmacy or shop reselling toothpaste
rationale: Category-level 'Зубная паста'.

intent: A household-goods shop reselling washing powder
rationale: The catalog splits powder by use: automatic machines, hand wash, universal. The query does not say, so all three are acceptable; automatic is the most common pack. Liquid detergent (03402003006) is a different product.

intent: A phone shop selling smartphones
rationale: Smartphones sit under 'Сотовые телефоны, радиотелефоны'; the catalog never uses the word 'смартфон' for the device itself.

intent: An electronics shop selling wireless earbuds
rationale: Category-level 'Наушники'.

intent: A phone accessories shop selling chargers
rationale: 'Зарядные устройства и блоки питания (всех видов и для всех устройств)'.

intent: A pharmacy or grocery reselling infant formula
rationale: Infant formula is 'Молочная смесь' under preparations for young children.

intent: A pet shop reselling cat food
rationale: 'Корма и кормовые добавки (всех видов), для домашних животных' is the pet-food line; the parent 'all kinds' code is defensible.

intent: A shop reselling AA batteries
rationale: Disposable batteries are 'Первичные батареи'; rechargeable ones would be accumulators (08507).

intent: A hardware shop reselling LED light bulbs
rationale: Bulbs are 'Лампы (всех видов)'. Many LED bulbs are nevertheless registered under 'Электрические лампы и светильники (всех видов)', so that code is defensible too.

intent: A building-materials shop reselling M400 cement bags without a named plant
rationale: Portland cement has no category-level code; unbranded M400 general-purpose variants are listed as attributes (D0, D5, D20, composite). M400 D20 is the common bag and is listed twice (240003 and 240007). With a known plant, the plant's branded code applies.

intent: A shop reselling 3-in-1 instant coffee sachets
rationale: Resold packaged goods, not a drink made on premises, so not the cafe code. The catalog files every 3-in-1 sachet (Maccoffee, Nescafe, Jacobs) under 'Молотый (порошкообразный) кофе'; 'Готовые продукты на основе ... кофе' matches the customs classification of coffee mixes and is defensible.

intent: A grocery reselling a 95 g jar of Nescafe Gold
rationale: Nescafe Gold is freeze-dried, so 'Сублимированный кофе: Nescafe, gold 95 гр' fits best, but the same product is also registered as 'Молотый (порошкообразный) кофе: Nescafe, голд 95 гр'. Both are real branded codes for it.

intent: A shop reselling instant cappuccino sachets (no brand given)
rationale: The make-vs-resell twin of the cafe cappuccino case: a sachet on a shelf is packaged coffee ('Молотый (порошкообразный) кофе', where Torabika and Nescafe cappuccino sachets live), not the catering coffee-drinks code.

intent: A shop reselling bottled iced coffee
rationale: Category-level 'Холодный кофе' under soft drinks; not the cafe coffee code.

intent: A shop reselling bags of chips
rationale: Potato chips (Lay's, Pringles, Cheers) are registered under 'Не замороженные овощи, приготовленные или консервированные без добавления уксуса...', a name nobody would guess. Corn and grain chips are 'Чипсы из злаков'. The query does not say which.

intent: A kiosk reselling a single Snickers bar
rationale: Branded code 'Шоколадный батончик: Snickers, батончик 50,5г'.

intent: A supermarket deli counter selling ready-made salads
rationale: A shop is not a catering establishment, so the catalog's separate 'Салаты (реализованный в торговых точках)' code applies, not the cafe salads code 10202001003.

intent: A filling station selling AI-92 petrol
rationale: 'Бензин марки АИ-92'; the 'неэтилированный' (unleaded) attribute code describes the same fuel and is equally acceptable.

intent: An Uzbek-speaking grocer selling chicken eggs
rationale: 'Tuxum' (egg) in a grocery means chicken eggs: category-level 'Куриные яйца'.

intent: A grocer selling top-grade wheat flour
rationale: 'Oliy nav' is top grade: 'Пшеничная мука высшего сорта'.

intent: A grocer selling rice
rationale: Rice from sacks sold by the kilo is 'Рис развесной'; bagged rice is 'Рис (расфасованный и упакованный)'. The query does not say which.

intent: A grocer selling table salt
rationale: 'Соль, пригодная для употребления в пищу'; industrial salt is a different code.

intent: A shop selling toilet paper
rationale: Category-level 'Бумага туалетная'; moist toilet paper (03401003001) is a different product.

intent: A shop selling packs of wet wipes
rationale: Wet wipes are 'Гигиенические салфетки (влажные и матирующие)'.

intent: A grocer selling butter
rationale: 'Сливочное масло (всех видов)'.

intent: A grocer typing in Uzbek Cyrillic selling cheese
rationale: 'Сыры (всех видов)'.

intent: A shop selling bars of soap
rationale: Plain soap for washing hands is 'Туалетное мыло'; laundry soap ('Хозяйственное мыло') is defensible for the bare word.

intent: A shop reselling ice cream from a freezer
rationale: Resold ice cream is 'Мороженое упакованное' (or 'весовое' when scooped by weight); not the cafe dessert code.

intent: An electronics shop with an English product list selling laptops
rationale: Category-level 'Ноутбук'.

intent: A pharmacy with an English product list selling sanitary pads
rationale: 'Гигиенические прокладки женские (в т.ч. мужские)'.

intent: A barbershop charging for a haircut
rationale: 'Услуги салонов красоты и парикмахерских (все виды услуг)' names hairdressers explicitly. The catalog also has a second 'Услуги салонов красоты' code in the arts-and-leisure group, which is defensible.

intent: A nail studio charging for a manicure
rationale: Nail services are beauty-salon services; the same two salon codes apply.

intent: A phone repair stall charging for a screen replacement
rationale: 'Услуги по ремонту и техническому обслуживанию мобильных устройств'. The spare part itself, if billed separately, is a goods line.

intent: A language centre selling a monthly English course
rationale: 'Услуги учебных и образовательных курсов, в том числе индивидуальное репетиторство (по всем направлениям)'.

intent: A private tutor invoicing maths lessons
rationale: The same courses code explicitly includes individual tutoring.

intent: A landlord invoicing monthly office rent
rationale: 'Услуги по аренде жилых и нежилых помещений' covers an office unit; 'аренде зданий и сооружений' is defensible when the whole building is rented.

intent: A business renting out apartments by the night
rationale: Short stays fit 'временного жилья ... в прочих местах кратковременного проживания (... гостиничные дома и др.)'. Treating it as residential rent ('аренде жилых и нежилых помещений') is also defensible; which one a tax inspector expects is unclear.

intent: A taxi company issuing a fiscal receipt for a ride
rationale: 'Услуга перевозки пассажиров на легковом автотранспорте (услуги нелинейного такси)'. Marshrutka (fixed-route taxi) is a different code.

intent: A trucking company billing a client for moving goods within Uzbekistan
rationale: Road freight 'по местным направлениям' for domestic hauls; the parent road-freight code is defensible. International legs have their own codes.

intent: A courier company charging for parcel delivery
rationale: 'Курьерская услуга'; 'Служба доставки товаров' is defensible for goods delivery.

intent: A cleaning company charging for an apartment clean
rationale: 'Услуги по уборке зданий, сооружений, помещений...(все виды услуг)'. 'Услуги по ведению домашнего хозяйства' is defensible for a housekeeper.

intent: A dry cleaner charging for cleaning a coat
rationale: 'Химическая чистка (химчистка)'.

intent: A gym selling a monthly membership
rationale: 'Услуги фитнес-центров и оздоровительных центров (все виды услуг)'; 'Тренажерный зал' is defensible for a pure gym.

intent: A private dental clinic billing a treatment
rationale: 'Услуги стоматолога по лечению и проведению процедур' for treatment; 'Консультация стоматолога' is right when only a consultation is billed.

intent: A massage studio adding massage to its price list
rationale: Non-medical massage is a salon service. The only code with the word 'массаж' is 'Реабилитационные услуги, Медицинский массаж', which is correct only for a licensed medical provider; it is included because the query alone cannot tell.

intent: A photographer charging for a photo shoot
rationale: 'Фото и видео услуги (все виды услуг)'.

intent: A web studio invoicing a website build
rationale: Software design and development ('Услуги по проектированию программного обеспечения ... разработке, внедрению'). The web/graphics/multimedia code 10399006 is defensible for design-only work.

intent: A SaaS company invoicing a monthly subscription
rationale: SaaS gives access rather than a licence copy: 'предоставлению ... третьим лицам доступа к программному обеспечению (базе данных)'. The licence/right-of-use code is defensible for per-seat licences.

intent: A wedding agency invoicing the organisation of a wedding
rationale: 'Комплексные услуги по проведению свадебных мероприятий, банкетов и других мероприятий'. The general events code 10715001 explicitly excludes weddings.

intent: An agency invoicing online advertising for a client
rationale: 'Услуги рекламы, в т.ч. продвижение товара'; the SMM/ICT-based services code 10399005 is defensible for social-media campaigns.

intent: An outsourced bookkeeper invoicing monthly accounting
rationale: 'Бухгалтерские услуги'. Accounting consulting (10602002) is a different service.

intent: A lawyer invoicing a legal consultation
rationale: 'Юридические консультации'. The general legal-services code 10601001002 explicitly excludes consultations.

intent: A car wash issuing a receipt
rationale: 'Услуги по чистке и мойке моторных транспортных средств (автомойка автомобилей)'.

intent: A tyre shop charging for fitting and balancing
rationale: There is no tyre-fitting code. Car maintenance 'все виды услуг' is the closest; 'Автомастерские услуги прочие' is defensible.

intent: A contractor invoicing a full apartment renovation
rationale: 'Услуги капитального и текущего ремонта помещений (комплексный ремонт, "под ключ")'; partial repair of a building is defensible.

intent: A private kindergarten charging monthly fees
rationale: A private kindergarten is 'Услуги негосударственного дошкольного образования'; the general pre-school code is defensible.

intent: A vet clinic charging for an examination
rationale: 'Услуги ветеринарные (все виды услуг)'.

intent: A driving school selling a course
rationale: 'Услуги автошколы'.

intent: A private school invoicing monthly tuition
rationale: 'Услуги негосударственного школьного образования'; the general school-education code is defensible.

intent: A hotel issuing a receipt for a night's stay
rationale: 'Гостиничные услуги (за проживание)'. The tourist (hotel) levy is a separate line (11199008003000001).

intent: A cafe owner misspelling cappuccino (double ч)
rationale: Same need as 'капучино': catering coffee drinks.

intent: A shawarma stall owner using the St Petersburg spelling
rationale: 'Шаверма' is a regional name for shawarma: catering fast food.

intent: A shopkeeper misspelling diapers
rationale: Typo of 'подгузники': category-level diapers code.

intent: A cafe owner typing cappuccino in Latin letters
rationale: Latin-script spelling of 'капучино': catering coffee drinks.

intent: A shopkeeper typing the Russian word for diapers on a Latin keyboard
rationale: Transliterated 'подгузники': category-level diapers code.

intent: A tea house typing samsa in Uzbek Cyrillic
rationale: Uzbek spelling of 'самса': flour-based main dish, fast food defensible.

intent: A tea house typing samsa in Uzbek Latin
rationale: Uzbek Latin 'somsa' = 'самса': flour-based main dish, fast food defensible.

intent: An Uzbek-speaking merchant, most likely a choyxona adding coffee to its menu, typing 'coffee' in Cyrillic
rationale: 'Қаҳва' means coffee. For a choyxona the catering coffee-drinks code is right, but the bare word does not say made vs resold, so the packaged-coffee category codes (ground/powder, beans, freeze-dried, extracts and concentrates) also count. This case tests script handling, not the make-vs-resell split. Chicory substitutes and coffee machines do not count.

intent: An Uzbek-speaking merchant, most likely a choyxona adding coffee to its menu, typing 'coffee' in Latin
rationale: Latin twin of 'қаҳва'; same acceptable set.

intent: A training centre typing 'study courses' with a plain ASCII apostrophe
rationale: Uzbek for 'study courses': the courses and tutoring code. Apostrophe variant: U+0027.

intent: The same training centre using the official Uzbek letter oʻ (U+02BB)
rationale: Same need; apostrophe variant U+02BB (modifier letter turned comma), the official orthography.

intent: The same training centre typing on a phone that inserts a curly quote (U+2018)
rationale: Same need; apostrophe variant U+2018 (left single quotation mark).

intent: A cafe owner with caps lock trouble typing cappuccino
rationale: Mixed case must not change the answer: catering coffee drinks.

intent: A barber misspelling haircut
rationale: Typo of 'стрижка': beauty salon and hairdresser services.

intent: A barbershop owner typing 'barbershop' in Uzbek Latin
rationale: 'Sartaroshxona' is a barbershop: hairdresser services.

intent: A barbershop owner typing 'barbershop' in Uzbek Cyrillic
rationale: Cyrillic twin of 'sartaroshxona'.

intent: A cafe typing lagman in Uzbek Cyrillic without the letter ғ
rationale: Uzbek 'лағмон' typed with г: same acceptable set as 'лагман'.

intent: A cafe typing lagman in Uzbek Latin with a curly apostrophe
rationale: Uzbek Latin 'lag'mon' (U+2018 apostrophe): same acceptable set as 'лагман'.

intent: A shop typing Coca-Cola phonetically in Latin letters
rationale: Any Coca-Cola product code counts (brand prefix 02202002001010, 83 SKUs); the pack size decides which one goes on the receipt.

intent: A phone repair stall misspelling 'телефона'
rationale: Typo of 'ремонт телефона': mobile device repair.

intent: An accountant pasting the IKPU from the tax committee's cafe guidance to confirm it
rationale: Exact code lookup must return that code.

intent: A salon owner pasting a code a consultant sent them
rationale: Exact code lookup.

intent: A shopkeeper pasting the category code for diapers from a supplier invoice
rationale: Exact code lookup of a category-level code.

intent: A shop copying the Coca-Cola 1.5 L code from a distributor's e-invoice
rationale: Exact code lookup of a branded code.

intent: A SaaS company checking the code its accountant chose
rationale: Exact code lookup of a service code.

intent: A shop copying the Nescafe cappuccino sachet code from an e-invoice
rationale: Exact code lookup.

intent: A pharmacy copying the Panadol 500 mg code from a supplier invoice
rationale: Exact code lookup in the pharmaceutical group.

intent: A shop scanning the barcode of a 1.5 L Coca-Cola bottle
rationale: The barcode is recorded on exactly this code.

intent: A kiosk scanning a Snickers bar
rationale: The barcode is recorded on exactly this code.

intent: A kiosk scanning a pack of Winston Blue
rationale: The barcode is recorded on 'Winston Blue' (the twin 'Blue' row carries a different barcode).

intent: A shop scanning an EAN-8 barcode on a Nescafe 3-in-1 sachet
rationale: Short EAN-8 barcode recorded on this code.

intent: A shop scanning a bag of Lay's salted chips
rationale: The barcode is recorded on this code (filed under 'Не замороженные овощи ...').

intent: A shop scanning a 12-digit UPC barcode on imported Voss water
rationale: UPC-A (12 digits, no leading zero) recorded on this code.

intent: An appliance shop scanning a HaYaL Thermo HY-RM 10L water heater
rationale: This barcode is recorded on two codes with the same name (the same model is listed three times); either is acceptable.

intent: An accountant typing the first 8 digits (cafe menu position) to browse all cafe codes
rationale: Any code under position 10202001 ('Меню общественного питания').

intent: An accountant typing a 5-digit class prefix (household services)
rationale: Any code under class 11702 (dry cleaning, salons, photo, childcare...).

intent: A shop typing an 11-digit sub-position prefix (soft drinks)
rationale: Any code under sub-position 02202002001 ('Безалкогольные напитки (газированные и негазированные)').

intent: A kiosk typing a 14-digit brand prefix (Winston cigarettes)
rationale: Any Winston cigarette code (brand prefix 02402001001009).

intent: A user typing a 3-digit group number (accommodation and catering services)
rationale: Any code in group 102.

intent: A phone shop typing the sub-position prefix for mobile phones
rationale: Any code under 08517001001 ('Сотовые телефоны, радиотелефоны').
